finalText:
5 files, small Node HTTP service. Flow:

**server.js** — HTTP entry. Pull `Authorization` header, verify via auth.js, pass to router. No token/no match → 401.

**auth.js** — HMAC bearer tokens, format `<userId>.<sig>`. Secret from `AUTH_SECRET` env (dev fallback). `verifyToken` checks sig with `timingSafeEqual` (no timing attack). `sign` exported for token issuing (not used inside repo — external tool must mint tokens).

**routes.js** — route table, method+path key (`GET /users`, `GET /orders`, `POST /orders`). Reads go through cache.js, writes hit store.js direct. Query parsed from URL search params; POST body expected in `q.body` but parseQuery never reads request body — **POST /orders likely broken**, body always undefined unless something else populates it.

**store.js** — in-memory Map, fake DB. Each record 15 min TTL from last write. `getUser`, `listOrders`, `putOrder`.

**cache.js** — LRU, 256 entries, no TTL of own. Read-through wrapper around store calls.

Gotcha worth knowing: routes.js comment claims writes "invalidate affected keys" but `putOrder` never touches cache — after first read, `orders:<userId>` cached forever (well, until LRU evicts), so new orders posted won't show in `GET /orders` till cache key evicted. Also cache has no TTL so it can outlive store's 15 min expiry, serving stale/expired-in-store data. Worth checking if intentional or bug before you build on top.

No test/build/package files present — just the 5 source files.
